subject: Architecture
title: Burj Khalifa: The World's Tallest Tower
description: A fast breakdown of Burj Khalifa: The World's Tallest Tower for builders.

hook.text: The Burj Khalifa stands 2,717 feet tall — over half a mile. It's visible from 60 miles away.

buildup.text: Its Y-shaped floor plan resists wind from all directions, like a tripod standing firm in a storm.

discovery.text: Workers poured concrete at night because daytime desert heat would crack it before it set properly.

twist.text: Dubai nearly went bankrupt during construction. Abu Dhabi bailed it out — and got the tower renamed.

climax.text: The Burj has the world's highest occupied floor, highest swimming pool, and highest observation deck.

punchline.text: Half a mile tall. Built at night. Named after a bailout.

quiz.question: Why was concrete poured at night during Burj Khalifa construction?
options: Desert heat would crack the concrete before it set
Nighttime labor costs were lower in Dubai

details.summary: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, completed in 2010, stands 828 meters tall — over 300 meters taller than its nearest competitor at the time. Its Y-shaped buttressed core design and stepped profile reduce wind vortices, while desert foundations reach 50 meters into sandy ground.
details.whyItMatters: The Burj Khalifa shattered height records and proved that engineering could reach nearly a kilometer. It established Dubai on the global stage and pushed structural engineering into genuinely new territory.
takeaways: Stands 828 meters tall, completed in 2010 in Dubai
Y-shaped plan and stepped profile reduce wind forces
Foundations reach 50 meters into desert sand

faq.question: How does the Burj Khalifa handle desert wind?
faq.answer: The Y-shaped plan confuses wind vortices that would cause dangerous oscillation in a symmetrical tower. The building steps back 26 times as it rises, so the wind profile changes at every level, preventing organized vortex shedding that causes swaying.

faq.question: What challenges did building in the desert present?
faq.answer: Extremely hot concrete had to be poured at night using ice-cooled water. Foundations go 50 meters into sandy soil with friction piles. The high-strength concrete at the base was specified at 80 MPa — among the strongest ever used in a building at that scale.
